items.title: August Lanoix Interview, 1961-04-19
items.q: [INTERVIEWER] What was your cousin's name, the Clarinet player? [INTERVIEWEE] Uh, Albert Gabriel. Oh yeah.

ctx.x: Well, I tell you, I had a cousin. He was a client at Flair. And he's the one who urged me to start music. Well, he had an old violin. He gave it to me. So I went to old man Hoffrey. And he told me, he said, you're wasting your time fooling around with an instrument like this. He said, because this instrument is not dying out. It's done dying out. So he advised me to take up the trombone. So that's why you settled on that. That's why I settled on the trombone.
What was your cousin's name, the Clarinet player?
